brief: A model reads a prompt and writes a reply.
body: Changing a setting, such as effort, does not swap in a different model.

brief: The text you send a model, including instructions and any source you attach.
body: A new chat receives only what that first message carries, unless you also bring a seed or a file.

brief: The text a model writes back.
body: It is counted apart from the prompt and from the hidden work.

brief: A chunk of text the product counts.
body: What you send, the hidden work, and the reply are counted apart.

brief: Work a model does before the reply you see.
body: Effort is the setting that allows more or less of it. Those tokens are counted apart from the prompt and the reply.

brief: A setting on a model for how much hidden work a turn may do.
body: This course uses low, medium, and high. Extra High waits until those three are familiar. The model stays the same.

brief: A conversation that resends its earlier turns with each follow-up.
body: A new chat does not, unless you carry forward what the next chat needs.

brief: How much of the current thread a product can still hold at once.
body: As the window fills, many products compress or compact the thread.

brief: A shortening of a thread you are staying in, done by the product as the context window fills.
body: Compaction is the same idea. The interface often says Compressing or Compacting, sometimes with a percent, and the pass usually takes a noticeable time.

brief: A short text, or a file, that carries one job's decisions into a new thread.
body: It is the handoff, not the whole transcript.

brief: A procedure written so a later chat can follow it without the transcript that produced it.
body: A seed carries one job. A skill carries a way of working you expect to repeat.

brief: The file many products ingest as a skill.
body: In the smallest case that file is the whole skill. A bundle may place other files beside it or in subfolders.

brief: A short structured block kept with a document such as SKILL.md.
body: It is often YAML. It may be general, or aimed at one model or one environment.

brief: A coding session in a terminal.
body: It is a thread that can also run tools. The session may be granted a project folder, and a new session does not keep the previous grant.

brief: One step in a session: the model does its work, may use a tool, and continues.
body: A turn cap limits how many steps one automated request may take. It is a different limit from the usage window.

brief: The side of a CLI session that reads files and takes the next step.
One clock on an allowance, with an amount and a reset.
body: Several clocks can run at once. A few-hour pause is a different clock from a weekly one.

brief: Two skills loaded for the same job.
body: The model may read both, spend tokens on both, and follow a mix when they disagree.

brief: A convention for what a file holds and how to read it, often shown by the ending of its name.
body: The ending is a hint. The contents still have to match. The linked entries are the list this course keeps so far, and the course page introduces them together.

brief: Text you can read in an editor without a special program.
body: Markdown, JSON, and YAML are plain text with extra rules. A file ending in .txt is plain text with no further format.

brief: A plain-text writing format that uses a small set of marks for headings, lists, and code.
body: These lessons are Markdown, and so is SKILL.md. The file ending is usually .md.

brief: A text format for structured data that a program can read without guessing.
body: Names and text sit in double quotes, inside braces for objects and square brackets for lists. The file ending is .json.

brief: A plain-text format for small structured data, often used as frontmatter beside a skill.
body: Indentation shows what belongs under what. A field is a name, a colon, and a value. The file ending is .yaml or .yml. It is looser than JSON, so a short block may be YAML while a file a program must read without guessing is JSON.

brief: A programming language. Helper scripts beside a skill are often Python files.
body: The file ending is .py.

brief: A file that packs other files into one, including their folders.
body: A skill bundle may travel as a zip, with SKILL.md at the top or in a subfolder. The file ending is .zip.

brief: In this course, the ability of computer programs and robots to mimic human intelligence.
body: People meet that ability in work, in education, and in everyday life. The subject strand is where the course stays with that idea.

brief: The information an AI system is given or produces.
body: Later items cover why quality and selection matter.
